source.title: Grokking phase transitions in learning local rules with gradient descent

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests grokking and related regularization and structure claims using analytically solvable perceptron models and tensor-network models trained on cellular-automaton rules, rather than reproducing the original transformer experiments.
record.gate_note: Included the paper's own analytic and experimental results on grokking times, regularization and effective dimension. The cited findings from other papers are not recorded as rows. Numerical values available only in plots are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: The paper builds solvable perceptron grokking models and trains tensor-network students on cellular-automaton rule 30 (an algorithmic task). It reports its own grokking times, measured as zero-test-error time minus zero-train-error time, and an effective-dimension progress measure. It uses a different method aimed at the same question as the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that grokking in their solvable models is a phase transition with computable critical exponents, grokking probability and grokking-time PDF, and that grokking is a consequence of the locality of the teacher rule. The fixed-attention rule-30 experiments roughly match the predicted critical exponent. L1 regularization gives higher grokking probability, shorter grokking time and lower effective dimension than L2. Training-loss spikes mark latent structural changes. Structure formation and grokking are linked on average but not per run.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies analytically specified separable perceptrons and shallow tensor-network attention models learning cellular-automaton rules, rather than transformers trained on modular arithmetic. It varies L1/L2 regularization and examines feature-space effective dimension.
record.method_sensitivity: Regularization type and strength affect grokking probability, grokking time, critical exponent and effective dimension; bond dimension and rule range are also varied. The paper notes that changing the initial distribution of the classification tensor can affect results.

fits_no_version.finding: Regularization type changes grokking behaviour. L1 shortens grokking time and time to zero test error more than L2. In the fixed-attention setup, L2 lowers the fraction of attention tensors that reach zero test error. In the D-ball analytic model, L2 raises that fraction up to a maximum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L1 regularization yields faster and more probable grokking than L2 weight decay in simple models.

fits_no_version.finding: Regularization lowers post-transition effective dimension, with L1 giving the lowest value.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-norm biases compress latent representations after grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-space structures differ across initializations (Figs. 16 vs 17), and training-loss spikes coincide with step changes in effective dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different runs reach different latent structures; loss spikes mark structural reorganizations.

record.problems: Several key experimental outcomes are shown in plots, with no reported uncertainty intervals. The full-model findings are averages over approximately 1000 initializations, while individual-run evidence is illustrative. The fixed-attention probability estimate uses rejection sampling and estimates over 20k random tensors. The analytical training-set-size trend is from a simplified separable-data perceptron, not an algorithmic dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying reported results were omitted.

untested.parts: Test accuracy starting at chance is not shown. Training-set size is not swept in the rule-30 experiments; the size trend comes only from the analytic perceptron models.
No Fourier or other generalizing circuit is identified, and removal of memorizing components is not measured.
No non-algorithmic data, no initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep, and no lazy-to-rich transition.
No efficiency comparison between memorizing and generalizing solutions, no critical dataset size, no ungrokking. The linear perceptron setup has no competing memorizing circuit.
Learned algorithms are not identified or compared across runs.
Adam is used throughout the full-model experiments with no optimizer or numerical-precision controls. The perceptron models use exact gradient flow but are not compared against the artifact claim.

missing.what: Full-model critical exponent of the test-error transition by regularizer: ν≈2.5 unregularized, ≈0.9 L2, ≈0.7 L1, nearly independent of d. This bears on how sharp the jump is.
Fixed-attention rule-30 experiments: second-order transitions with ν≈0.72–0.86 independent of λ, bimodal grokking-time PDFs, and longer grokking time with larger Deff.
2- and 3-local rules: grokking time grows with rule range K (e.g. unregularized 3-local tG 1.85–2.38 vs 1-local 0.60–0.77). L1 again shortens tG; L2 sometimes lengthens it.
D-dimensional ball analytic model: grokking probability rises with N and class separation and falls exponentially with dimension D.
Mean zero-test-error times t_eps for each regularizer and d. These exist only inside row values; they need their own rows.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T2: toy perceptron and tensor-network models on rule 30, not transformers on modular arithmetic. The full-model 'delay' is moderate and is defined relative to zero train error. The paper never shows test accuracy starting at chance. The text and the Fig. 18 legend disagree on the L2 size trend: the text says grokking time increases with d, but the legend shows 0.60, 0.54, 0.33. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: The local-rule experiments do not establish that initial test accuracy is at chance while training accuracy saturates, and the full tensor-network experiments do not sweep training-set size. The training-set-size trend comes from the paper's solvable 1D perceptron model, not a modular-arithmetic task.

The paper does not identify a Fourier circuit or memorizing components, or directly measure their removal. Its effective-dimension results are structural proxies, including averages over initializations.
No non-algorithmic image, text or molecule task, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
The paper does not test whether regularization produces a more efficient generalizing circuit, nor a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.
Different feature-space structures across runs are discussed, but the paper does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs.
The paper uses Adam in its full-model experiments but does not control for adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point softmax limits.
